title: Heat stress links to coral bleaching were uncertain in Indian Ocean surveys matched by month in 2003-2019
abstract: We tested whether heat stress links to coral bleaching repeat across oceans and time periods after control for survey location and timing. We used Reef Check observations in version 2 of the Global Coral-Bleaching Database. The main model used 6,217 site-month records from 1,411 repeat sites in 1998-2019. It gave 3.85 percentage points more bleaching per four degree-heating weeks (95% interval 0.97 to 6.72). Separate ocean estimates were positive. A stricter model compared the same calendar month at each site. In that model the Indian Ocean estimate was -0.49 points (-8.26 to 7.27), from 170 records at 51 sites in 2003-2019. The pooled estimate remained positive at 3.88 points (0.31 to 7.45). The Indian estimate was also near zero on the same selected records without month controls. The earlier period estimate also included zero. Thus a positive pooled link did not give clear replication in every region and time period. These are observational estimates. Survey selection, small region counts, and limited heat stress variation prevent a causal claim. Air pollution and species-level change were not tested.
